items.description: Confirm the claimed top-level subsystem, source snapshot, scope boundaries, research questions, and common terminology for all sections.
items.expectedOutput: Approved scope brief and shared glossary.

items.description: Write the executive summary, introduction, studied-system context, subsystem-selection rationale, research questions, and report roadmap.
items.expectedOutput: Integrated opening section of approximately 1.5–2 pages.

items.description: Collect all sections and diagrams, remove duplication, enforce one terminology and citation style, and keep the report within 10–15 pages.
Publish the report and related web-accessible artifacts on the Group H website and verify every internal and external link.
items.expectedOutput: Readable online report with working related-content links.

items.description: Export and verify the final PDF, coordinate the final team review, and submit it before Sunday, November 15 at 11:59 PM.
items.expectedOutput: Verified final report PDF and confirmed submission.

items.description: Record the OpenPilot v0.9.5 source snapshot, Understand project settings, languages, entity types, extracted relations, exclusions, and limitations.
Explain the extraction and grouping process from source entities through relations, subsystem assignments, hierarchical composition, and cleaned views.
Create the top-level file/entity-to-subsystem mapping table and document every manual grouping rule and unresolved classification.
items.expectedOutput: Reviewed mapping table and decision log.

items.description: Redraw the system-level concrete architecture with hierarchy, major relations, a legend, scope note, and traceable evidence identifiers.
items.expectedOutput: Report-ready system architecture diagram with editable source.

items.description: Write the methodology and system-level architecture section with figures, captions, evidence references, limitations, and a handoff to the focused subsystem analysis.
Validate the selected subsystem's file and entity membership and decompose it into meaningful sub-subsystems where evidence supports the grouping.
items.expectedOutput: Reviewed focused hierarchy and membership inventory.

items.description: Describe the selected subsystem's responsibilities, important entities, internal organization, entry points, outputs, and external boundaries.
Identify important internal and external dependencies and trace each major relation to the functions or entities that cause it.
Create a subsystem hierarchy diagram and focused dependency diagram with consistent names, evidence identifiers, legends, and captions.
items.expectedOutput: Two report-ready static diagrams with editable sources.

items.description: Write the focused subsystem structure and dependency-analysis section, including surprising relations, limitations, and unresolved questions.
Choose one important scenario that exercises the selected subsystem and document its actors, trigger, preconditions, main behavior, alternatives, and result.
Trace the scenario through calls, state changes, control flow, or data flow using Understand and source evidence.
Create a readable sequence diagram and, when useful, a state diagram that use the same entities and boundaries as the static architecture.
items.expectedOutput: Report-ready dynamic diagram set with editable sources.

items.description: Identify the supported architectural style and noteworthy design patterns, clearly separating extracted evidence from interpretation.
Write the dynamic behavior, architectural style, and design-pattern section with figures, captions, evidence links, and limitations.
Compare the recovered subsystem with Group H's Assignment 1 conceptual model and classify convergences, divergences, and absences.
Investigate likely reasons for important gaps without presenting inferred developer intent as fact.
Analyze alternatives, trade-offs, limitations, threats to validity, lessons learned, and what the team would do differently.
Audit claims, evidence labels, citations, diagrams, captions, terminology, accessibility, and page-budget compliance across the full report.
items.expectedOutput: Independent quality-review record and resolved issue list.

items.description: Write the comparison, trade-offs, limitations, lessons, and conclusion; consolidate and verify the final reference list.
items.expectedOutput: Completed 2–2.5 page closing package and references.
